born.why: The code analyzes the agent's personal history for each item type, calculating a risk score based on past n1 increases. It avoids any item that has previously caused n1 to rise, prioritizing items like k=431 and k=433 which have consistently reduced or stabilized n1, thereby keeping the agent alive longer by minimizing risk exposure.

The code prioritizes survival by blocking actions when n1 is high (>60) and uses historical performance of specific item types (k) to filter out consistently losing items, preventing unnecessary accumulation of n1 from unfavorable risks.

This code strictly avoids the dangerous k=110 item which consistently raises n1, prevents taking items that trigger a rejection (n5='a2') unless necessary for survival, and uses an emergency abort at critical n1 levels to preserve life.

The original code blindly followed the default choice `x.n5`, which led to high n1 values (near death). The new code checks if n1 is critically high (>40 or >30) and overrides the default with a safer option 'a3' to prevent death, while still respecting the default choice when n1 is safe. It also implements an approach strategy that stops approaching if n1 gets too high, prioritizing survival over gathering.

The previous code blindly followed the default choice, leading to repeated exposure to deadly item k=233 (which raised n1 significantly).
